voyage.name: Osaka Science Museum
voyage.price: Adults ¥400, university and high school students ¥300, children free, additional charges for planetarium
voyage.hours: Tue-Sun 09:30-17:00, closed Dec 28-Jan 4, closed on public holidays
voyage.content: Big interactive activity center on several floors. Great for kids. Planetarium and cinema (with science films) downstairs.

voyage.name: Osaka Museum of Housing and Living
voyage.alt: ja 大阪くらしの今昔館 Ōsaka kurashi no Konjaku-kan
voyage.price: Adults ¥600, free for junior-high students, kids, and seniors
voyage.content: Step back in time as you walk through this life-sized reproduction of an Osaka neighborhood from the 1830s. The street contains re-creations of a public bath (you can borrow a yukata, or cotton kimono, to wear as you stroll around), as well as various shops and merchants' living quarters. There's also a section displaying detailed dioramas of Osaka after the Meiji Period. English-language audio guides are available.

voyage.name: Umeda Sky Building
voyage.price: Adult ¥2000, children 4-12 ¥500, 50% reduction for those with a disability certificate
voyage.content: Built in an attempt to upgrade Osaka's somewhat downbeat Kita district, the project wasn't quite the hoped-for commercial success but this bizarrely shaped 40-story, 173-m building is still a city landmark. Take the escalator through midair to the rooftop observatory for an open-air view of Osaka, which is particularly impressive on a clear night. There is a lover's seat, where if you hold your partner's hand, and ea

voyage.name: Japan Mint and Mint Museum
voyage.content: It's not widely known even by people from elsewhere in the country that Japan Mint is headquartered in Osaka. For Osakans, Sakura-no-tōrinuke (桜の通り抜け, cherry blossom tunnel road) is a synonym for this facility, attracting a large number of visitors (close to 1 million in just 7 days) during a limited, planned week in mid-Apr. A must-see if you are fond of nature and happen to drop into Osaka in-season. The museum is

voyage.name: Osaka Shiki Musical Theater
voyage.content: Home of the Shiki Theatre Company, proposing plays and musicals.

voyage.name: Zepp Namba
voyage.content: A pop club, capacity 2500.

voyage.name: Billboard Live Osaka
voyage.alt: ビルボードライブ大阪
voyage.address: Kita Ward, Umeda, 2 Chome−2−22 ハービスPLAZA ENT 地下 2階 B204 nuna 梅田
voyage.content: A jazz club, formerly "Blue Note Osaka".

voyage.name: Daimaru Umeda
voyage.content: One of the largest department stores in Osaka.

voyage.name: Hankyu Sanban-gai
voyage.content: The large shopping areas filled with a variety of shops from cages to brandname boutiques.

voyage.name: Herbis Plaza ENT
voyage.content: Boutiques of famous brands inside and outside Japan, gourmet restaurants.

voyage.name: Snack Park
voyage.content: Offers okonomiyaki, takoyaki and a few surprises like doteyaki (どて焼き) — stewed beef sinew.

voyage.name: Tsuruhashi Fūgetsu
voyage.content: Good okonomiyaki as well as yakisoba, with extra toppings (egg, cheese, etc.). The restaurant overlooks Umeda. There's an English menu.

voyage.name: Hanadako
voyage.content: Standing or to-go takoyaki, very popular with the locals.

voyage.name: En (Umeda)
voyage.price: Food will cost ¥2000-2500 per person, drinks start from around ¥500
voyage.content: En is one of the most atmospheric and tastiest izakayas in Osaka, with branches in Umeda and Namba. The interior is beautiful and food is delicious and reasonably priced. En also has a large range of Japanese sake and has an English menu.

voyage.name: Torikizoku
voyage.content: Torikizoku is the most popular yakitori chain in Kansai, and can be found near most major stations in Osaka. The food is delicious, comes in generous serves and is very cheap. It's very popular with both locals and expats, and is always busy. Try to come before 7:30PM to secure seats.

voyage.name: Endo Sushi
voyage.content: Sushi place in Osaka's fish market.

voyage.name: Harukoma honten
voyage.content: Sushi restaurant located in the Tenjinbashisuji shopping street. Whenever they are open, there is a line outside, mainly composed of locals, so be prepared for a wait of an hour or more.

voyage.name: Lupu
voyage.content: A gay and lesbian bar owned by a lesbian couple.

voyage.name: Cafe de Jumpin' Jumpin'
voyage.content: One of Osaka's gay and lesbian bars.

voyage.name: Explosion
voyage.content: Osaka's most popular and largest (albeit still not very big) gay club. They hold special events on Fridays and Saturdays, some of which are men-only and occasionally women-only, so check their website to make sure that you will be able to enter on the day you plan to visit. Foreigners sometimes get discounts or extra free drink coupons, so bring identification (especially if you are of Asian descent).

voyage.name: Jack in the Box
voyage.content: A men-only gay nightclub.

voyage.name: Sam and Dave
voyage.content: Popular international dance club with a meat-market vibe. Two locations in Osaka.

voyage.name: J-Hoppers Osaka Central
voyage.price: 8 or 6 bed dorm ¥2500, private rooms ¥3000 per person
voyage.content: A lively backpackers hostel in the central Osaka. There are three kinds of private rooms (twin, double and triple room). All staff members speak English and can help guests making travel plans. There are also staff who speak French and German. Free WiFi with your laptop or ¥100 per 30 min. for hostel computers. Rental bikes (¥500 per day), with no curfew or lockout and held-luggage services.

voyage.name: New Japan Umeda
voyage.price: ¥2700 for a night, ¥3300 including spa entry
voyage.content: Formerly known as Capsule Inn Osaka. This is Japan's first capsule hotel, designed by noted architect Kisho Kurokawa and opened in 1979. Still open for business, happy to accommodate male foreigners with some semblance of a clue and a steal of a price. No women allowed.

voyage.name: Daitoyo
voyage.content: Near Umeda, with branches at Namba and Juso. It has a hot spring spa, sauna, and a floor for women.

voyage.name: Sunplaza Rinkai
voyage.price: ¥3500 per person per apartment inclusive of taxes, service charges and utilities
voyage.content: Website is in Japanese. The English site can be obtained through an online booking agent if you Google its full name and if vacancies are available an immediate confirmation will be given. Twins beds available. Each apartment has in-suite shower and toilet, A/C, TV, and a kitchenette complete with fridge, stove and cooking utensils.

voyage.name: Hilton Osaka
voyage.content: Across the street from JR Osaka station.

voyage.name: Hotel Granvia Osaka
voyage.content: Next to the JR Osaka Train Station.

voyage.name: Imperial Hotel
voyage.content: At riverside.

voyage.name: Rihga Royal Hotel
voyage.content: Opened as the New Osaka Hotel in 1935, this landmark hotel proudly offers one of the best hotel services in town.

voyage.name: Ritz-Carlton
voyage.content: Japan's first. This particular outlet was voted the best hotel in Japan several times, and has become known as one of the city's swankiest dining and meeting points. Rates start around ¥30,000 a night and rise skyward from there.

voyage.name: The Westin Osaka
voyage.content: Next to the Umeda Sky Building.

voyage.name: Kamigata Ukiyoe Museum
voyage.content: (上方浮世絵館) A rather small museum in Nanba dedicated to ukiyoe, Japanese woodblock prints. The interior of the museum looks a bit like an adobe house. It may be most interesting to someone already familiar with the art, as the information inside mostly Japanese only.

voyage.name: Sumo Spring Grand Tournament
voyage.content: The Osaka Tournament of Japan's national sport, sumo wrestling, is usually held mid-March annually at Osaka Prefectural Gymnasium. Check for schedules and ticket availabilities at the official Nihon Sumo Kyokai homepage.

voyage.name: National Bunraku Theater
voyage.content: One of the last places in the world where bunraku, a form of intricate puppet theater from the Edo period, can be seen live. The large puppets, which require three operators each, are accompanied by traditional music and narration, and act out great Japanese plays of the 1600s and 1700s. Transcripts in Japanese and synopses in English are provided.

voyage.name: ROR Comedy
voyage.content: English-language stand-up comedy playhouse.

voyage.name: The Silver Ball Planet
voyage.alt: ザ・シルバーボールプラネット
voyage.content: Pinball arcade featuring over 100 retro, classic & modern pinball machines. ¥100 per play (3 balls) typically, but some are as cheap as ¥10

voyage.name: Tamago-yaki stand
voyage.content: Best for a snack, this outdoor stall offers a hard-to-find and delicious treat called tamago-yaki, fried egg atop a wide flat sembei cracker with sauce and a variety of toppings available. Much tastier than it sounds.

voyage.name: Tsuruhashi Fūgetsu
voyage.content: Good okonomiyaki and yakisoba, with extra toppings (egg, cheese, etc.). The restaurant overlooks Umeda. There's an English menu.

voyage.name: Tako Tako King
voyage.content: This takoyaki place has very friendly staff. Look for the big red octopus wearing a crown.

voyage.name: En (Namba)
voyage.address: 大阪市中央区難波千日前 12-30 難波長和ビル4F
voyage.content: The Namba branch of the excellent En izakaya (see above).

voyage.name: Torikizoku
voyage.content: Torikizoku is the most popular yakitori chain in Kansai, and can be found near most major stations in Osaka. The food is delicious, comes in generous serves and is very cheap. It's very popular with both locals and expats, and is always busy. Try to come before 19:30 to secure seats.

voyage.name: Ajinoya
voyage.address: Namba 1-7-16 現代こいさんビル2F
voyage.content: Some of the best okonomiyaki in Osaka, and they're so proud of it they prepare it for you from start to end, making a good choice for the casual visitor as well. The "A set" (¥5,900) includes no less than four styles and will leave four people stuffed to the gills. Very popular, so join the queue early, and beware that ordering here is once and done: you can't add on more later.

voyage.name: Melbourne Coffee
voyage.address: 1st Floor Sanei Moor Building, 3-8-7 Minamisenba Chuo-ku
voyage.content: Australian café, serving all day breakfast.

voyage.name: Harijyu
voyage.content: Shabu-shabu or sukiyaki in Japanese tatami rooms. No reservations are taken except for large groups, so arrive early at nights (18:00 or so) to be sure you get a room without waiting.

voyage.name: Kani Dōraku
voyage.content: Now a nationwide chain, but this is the original -- although there are three branches around Dotonbori alone! Easily identifiable by the giant mechanical crab waving its pincers about, and as you might guess, the speciality here is crab. The menu runs to pages and pages of ways to prepare the crustaceans, ranging from sushi to hotpots to gratin, but perhaps the most Japanese way is to order o-tsukuri (sashimi) and tr

voyage.name: Bar Kama Sutra
voyage.content: Small cozy karaoke bar is almost impossible to find but well worth the effort. Foreign and English-speaking Japanese staff, and over 130,000 songs to choose from. The owner, Richard, is a long term resident of Japan and is a wealth of information on what to do and see in the area, where to stay and even where to find work. (No "u" in e-mail address is correct, or: richosaka@gmail.com.)

voyage.name: Blarney Stone
voyage.content: This pair of Irish pubs have a laid-back atmosphere, friendly staff, and a decent happy hour.

voyage.name: Blarney Stone Shinsaibashi
voyage.address: Chuo-ku, Higashi Shinsaibashi 2-5-27, Kohda Bldg. B1

voyage.name: HUB
voyage.content: This British pub chain is at many locations around Osaka, including along Midosuji street in Shinsaibashi, in Namba, and in Chayamachi (Umeda, east side of Hankyu station and walk north a little). HUB serves as a meeting place for many expats as well as Japanese locals. Get there early for happy hour discounts on cocktails (17:00-19:00).

voyage.name: G Physique
voyage.content: One of Osaka's most popular gay and lesbian bars among foreigners.

voyage.name: Club Life
voyage.address: Gold Center Building B1F 2-8-12 Higashi Shinsaibashi
voyage.content: Great place to listen to Hip Hop, R&B, Reggae and all black music. Beside playing the latest music, you can also listening the old school classics. Enjoy a wide range of drinks to get you in the party mood or help you relax.

voyage.name: Clube Joule
voyage.content: Packed with trance lovers.

voyage.name: Club Pure
voyage.price: Cover ¥4000 men, ¥2500 women; includes unlimited drinks but don't lose your cup
voyage.content: Extremely crowded dance club. The crowd is around 25-30% international. Be sure to bring your passport, as the ID check here is atypically rigorous. The closest subway station is Namba Station, which is about 5-10 min walk. No dancing is allowed in the club.

voyage.name: Guest House U-en
voyage.content: The ground floor of this building was once a printing factory, and the upper level was a family home. The guest house has a traditional atmosphere.

voyage.name: Asahiplaza Shinsaibashi
voyage.content: Sauna available, and there is a separate area for women.

voyage.name: B&S Eco-Cube Shinsaibashi
voyage.content: Sauna available, and there is a separate area for women.

voyage.name: Azu-Garden Nippombashi
voyage.price: Single ¥4,200, double ¥9030, twin ¥9,030 per apartment. All rates inclusive of taxes
voyage.content: Online reservation site in English here but you may or may not get a response. If no response, try an online booking agent.

voyage.name: Kaneyoshi Ryokan
voyage.content: This comfortable, modern ryokan is in the heart of downtown on the riverside of Dotombori and very close to the Osaka shopping quarter. English website has an online reservation system.

voyage.name: Weekly Green in Namba
voyage.alt: ウィークリーグリーンINナンバ
voyage.price: Single ¥4200, twin ¥9450, triple ¥14490, quad ¥18900 per apartment. All rates inclusive of service charge & consumption tax
voyage.content: English website has an online reservation system. It claims to have English-speaking staff on its website so you may attempt an online reservation. If no response, try an online booking agent. Each apartment equipped with in-suite shower and toilet, kitchenette, fridge, portable cooking stove, A/C, TV and telephone.

voyage.name: Comfort Inn Shinsaibashi
voyage.content: 2 blocks east of Shinsaibashi's central covered shopping arcade, this hotel is a little better than the average business hotel, with clean rooms, English-speaking staff, and a free, generous breakfast buffet.

voyage.name: Il Cuore
voyage.price: Single ¥9,000 with a double bed for one or two guests
voyage.content: This is a slightly nicer business hotel with larger than average rooms. The hotel provides English language instructions for laundry machines and other hotel services. Breakfast an additional ¥ 1,000.

voyage.name: Yamatoya Honten
voyage.content: A Japanese-style hotel in Dotonbori. There are staff members who can speak English.

voyage.name: Best Western Hotel Fino Osaka Shinsaibashi
voyage.content: About 5 minutes walking distance from the Shinsaibashi shopping area. Some staff speak good English. The rooms are very small, but very clean.

voyage.name: Fraser Residence Nankai
voyage.content: Compact but airy and comfortable studio, 1 and 2-bedroom apartments right across the street from Nankai Namba station. Full kitchen and washing facilities make this a great choice for longer stays.

voyage.name: Hotel Nikko Osaka
voyage.content: Huge Landmark Hotel smack in the middle of Shinsaibashi along tree lined Mido-suji Avenue. Rooms are comfortable and have amazing views at night as hotel is the tallest building in the immediate area. Attached to Shinsaibashi train station and close to Amerika-mura, shopping, and night-life.

voyage.name: Hotel New Otani Osaka
voyage.content: A luxury business hotel in Osaka, Japan offering accommodation, 13 restaurants and bars, vacation packages and meeting rooms. This five-star hotel is in the Osaka Business Park near Osaka Castle.

voyage.name: Swissôtel Nankai
voyage.content: Next to Namba train and bus stations.

voyage.name: Osaka Castle
voyage.price: Adults ¥1200, university/high school students ¥600, children 15 and below free
voyage.content: Osaka's best known sight, although it's a concrete reconstruction that pales in comparison with, say, Himeji. Think of it as a museum built in the shape of a castle, rather than as an historical Japanese castle, as the interior consists of several gloomy modern galleries rather than a real reconstruction. Still, it's pretty enough from the outside, especially in the cherry blossom season when Osakans flock to the cas

voyage.name: Osaka Museum of History
voyage.hours: Mon-Thu 09:30-17:00, Fri 09:30-20:00, closed Tue, or Wed if Tue is a holiday
voyage.content: An ideal place to learn all-abouts of Osaka's history. Enjoyable view over Osaka Castle and the OBP skyscrapers.

voyage.name: Peace Osaka
voyage.alt: 大阪国際平和センター
voyage.content: A museum dedicated to the promotion of peace through displays of war. Because it is an Osaka museum, it largely focuses on the effects of the bombings on Osaka in World War II. In the past, the museum also had exhibitions depicting the atrocities committed by Japan against China, Korea, and Southeast Asia. Sadly, however, those exhibitions were permanently removed in 2015 in response to pressure from conservative pol

voyage.name: National Bunraku Theater
voyage.alt: 国立文楽劇場 (Kokuritsu Bunraku Gekijō)
voyage.content: One of the last places in the world where bunraku, a form of intricate puppet theater from the Edo period, can be seen live. The large puppets, which require three operators each, are accompanied by traditional music and narration, and act out great Japanese plays of the 1600s and 1700s. Transcripts in Japanese and synopses in English are provided.

voyage.name: Jo-Terrace
voyage.content: A cluster of midrange restaurants and cafes in an attractive wooden complex inspired by a traditional jōkamachi, the shopping district below a castle. A good place for a post-castle coffee or meal.

voyage.name: CarpeDiem Inn
voyage.content: Traditional-style house and garden within walking distance of the Shiroyama Temple.

voyage.name: Super Hotel Osaka Tanimachi 4-Chome
voyage.content: Mid-price chain hotel, around a corner from the Tanimachi 4-chome subway station and a 7-Eleven store with ATM that accepts foreign cards. Modern and clean but compact rooms, with a free Japanese breakfast and free WiFi included with all stays.

voyage.name: Open Air Museum of Old Farmhouses
voyage.alt: 日本民家集落博物館 (nihon minka shūraku hakubutsukan)
voyage.content: Ryokuchi park is lovely, and in it is a museum of a dozen old Edo period farmhouses, moved across country and lovingly reconstructed. Also on display are tools, furniture, and the like. You can go to Himeji-jo or the old palace in Kyoto and see how the rulers lived, but come down here to see how the people lived. Thanks to the efforts of a volunteer from Australia, they have a great new English-language brochure to g

voyage.name: Osaka municipal indoor pool - Yodogawa
voyage.alt: 大阪市立淀川屋内プール
voyage.content: Heated swimming pool & exercise room.

voyage.name: Shin-Osaka Youth Hostel
voyage.content: A clean, modern, and friendly youth hostel.

voyage.name: Mystays Shin Osaka
voyage.price: Web site lists singles starting from ¥8300, though cheaper rates might be found when searching for availability
voyage.content: Small, clean rooms and a bit of a hike to the bullet train station, but unbeatable for the price. Some staff speak English. Some rates include buffet breakfast in the hotel's restaurant (¥1100 separately). Family Mart and Lawson convenience stores are a half-block away, while there is a 7-Eleven with international ATM access is on the way from Shin-Osaka station.

voyage.name: Sumiyoshi Grand Shrine
voyage.content: One of Japan's oldest Shinto shrines, with a history stretching back 1800 years. Its traditional architecture is unusual among Japan's shrines, and its park-like surroundings with the sacred bridge arching over a tranquil pond make it a restful break from the busy environment of Osaka.

voyage.name: Tobita Shinchi
voyage.content: This is Japan's largest red-light district outside Tokyo, where ladies pose at genkan entrances Amsterdam-style to attract clientele, accompanied by an older woman (called a yarite-baba or mama-san) who serves as the pimp and collects money from customers. However, this place is arguably more interesting to walk through than its Amsterdam counterpart, and most of the brothels operate out historic buildings dating bac

voyage.name: Cerezo Osaka
voyage.content: The local J. League soccer team plays at Nagai Stadium.

voyage.name: Nagai Stadium
voyage.alt: ヤンマースタジアム長居
voyage.content: Nagai Stadium is the home of the professional soccer team Cerezo Osaka.

voyage.name: Taiyoshi Hyakuban
voyage.content: Most of the "restaurants" in the area are really brothels in disguise (since prostitution is illegal in Japan), but this extravagant century-old brothel is a Tangible Cultural Property that has been turned into an actual restaurant open to the public. Specialities include hot pot dishes like sukiyaki and yosenabe.

voyage.name: For Leaves Inn Nagai
voyage.alt: フォーリーブスイン長居

voyage.name: Hiro's Guesthouse
voyage.price: Dormitory ¥2500, private rooms ¥3500 per person, free Wifi and computer use
voyage.content: Hiro's Guesthouse is in the heart of Koreatown in Osaka. It is a little far from the station, but in a nice, social neighbourhood. The open first floor of the guesthouse is very social and great to hang out and make friends at. Hiro and the others go out of their way to help and ensure you have a good time - this is more than just a place to sleep at.

voyage.name: Osaka Municipal Nagai Youth Hostel
voyage.alt: 大阪市立長居ユースホステル
voyage.price: ¥3000 per person per night, ¥1000 dinner, ¥500 breakfast

voyage.name: Nagai Park Hotel
voyage.price: Single room: ¥6500 per person per night including breakfast. Twin room: ¥6500 per person per night including breakfast

voyage.name: Tempozan Harbor Village
voyage.alt: 天保山ハーバービレッジ
voyage.content: Plaza and shopping centre, which houses an aquarium, Ferris wheel, an art gallery, Legoland and a cruise terminal. On the weekend, musicians and street performers offer additional entertainment to people outside the aquarium.

voyage.name: Osaka Aquarium Kaiyukan
voyage.price: 2700 JPY adults (16 and over, high school), 1400 JPY child (7-15, elementary school and junior high-school), infant (4-6) 700 JPY
voyage.content: This is one of the world's largest aquariums, with 11,000 tons of water and plenty of sharks (including a whale shark), dolphins, otters, seals, and other sea creatures. The largest tank, representing the Pacific Ocean with 5,400 tons is nothing but overwhelming. Can get intensely crowded, but the aquarium is a spiral featuring the same tanks, and crowds thin out as you get to deeper views of each tank. Back Stage Vi

voyage.name: Tempozan Ferris Wheel
voyage.content: One of the largest Ferris wheels, overlooking Osaka Bay and surrounding areas such as Mount Ikoma to the east, Akashi Kaikyō Bridge to the west, Kansai International Airport to the south, and the Rokko Mountains to the north. 17-minute ride. There is an option of a gondola with a see-through floor for no additional cost, but lines for these gondolas tend to be dramatically longer as they are fewer and in greater dema

voyage.name: Legoland Discovery Center Osaka
voyage.alt: レゴランド・ディスカバリー・センター大阪

voyage.name: Naniwa Kuishinbo Yokocho
voyage.alt: なにわ食いしんぼ横丁
voyage.content: Food theme park (or food court, depending on who you ask), with an aesthetic and theme of nostalgia for the 1960s streets of Osaka. Various Osaka delicacies are available here, including Takoyaki, Okonomiyaki, Kushikatsu, and Ikayaki.

voyage.name: Maishima Sludge Center and Maishima Incineration Plant
voyage.content: Without a doubt, the best sludge center you've ever seen. The incineration plant makes other waste facilities look like dumps. These two buildings were designed by eccentric Austrian architect Friedensreich Hundertwasser. They are fantastical works that have to be seen to be believed. There are display panels in the lobby of the sludge centre. Tours are available if you contact the facilities in advance, but Hundertw

voyage.name: Maishima Pottery Village
voyage.price: 1-day workshop for hand forming ¥500–3500. Additional charge for shipping your work. Booking required.
voyage.content: Maishima Pottery Village opened in Osaka’s manmade island in 1998 for the education and promotion of naniwazuyaki, made from the vast amounts of unwanted marine clay which resulted from the construction of Kansai International Airport. The main building has studios with electric and momentum potter’s wheels, rooms for preparing clay and glazes, a gallery, a noborigama climbing kiln and an anagama tunnel kiln. There a

voyage.name: Boat Race Suminoe
voyage.price: General admission ¥100, reserved seating for additional charge
voyage.content: There's no "bettor" place to see one of Japan's unique gambling sports, hydroplane boat racing, than the race course that typically helps crown the sport's champion every December. If you're interested in placing a bet, you might want to do some research at the official multilingual site of the sport, as there is practically no English guidance available once you arrive.

voyage.name: Takopa (Takoyaki Park)
voyage.price: Admission free, Octopus dumpling ball available for sale at 6 stores
voyage.content: Visitors can sample fare from six leading takoyaki shops that Osakans, famously particular about their takoyaki, unreservedly recommend.

voyage.name: Hotel Fukuracia Osaka Bay
voyage.alt: ホテルフクラシア大阪ベイ

voyage.name: Osaka Joytel Hotel
voyage.alt: 大阪ジョイテルホテル

voyage.name: Art Hotel Osaka Bay Tower
voyage.alt: アートホテル大阪ベイタワー
